transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-01
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Carlos Ramirez (Meridian - Head of Cloud), Anita Patel (Meridian - Security), Michael O'Neill (Meridian - Program Manager), Zoe Kim (Meridian - DevOps)

Summary: weekly pilot security sync; reviewed audit logging artifact, SSO/SAML integration status, data retention for pilot, SOC2 documentation request, and network/VPC peering items. Agreed on next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the weekly security sync for the pilot, quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Carlos Ramirez: hi carlos here, head of cloud at meridian
[00:00:08] Anita Patel: anita, security eng
[00:00:10] Michael O'Neill: michael program manager
[00:00:12] Zoe Kim: zoe devops
[00:00:14] Priya Nandakumar: priya from redwood se
[00:00:16] Liam Ortiz: liam from cs
[00:00:18] Jordan Lee: great thanks. quick agenda: audit logs and retention, SSO progress, SOC2 and security docs, network peering checklist and any blockers. we've got ~45 minutes so we'll go through items and capture action items.

[00:01:02] Anita Patel: quick thing up front, we had a question on the last email about whether redwood will surface per-token request identifiers in the audit logs; we need item-level correlation for any requests that touch PII for our compliance trail.
[00:01:18] Priya Nandakumar: yes, good callout. the runtime emits a request_id and session_id in the audit logs; right now in the pilot logging we've enabled request_id, user_id and model_name. the only gap i saw is we haven't yet included full prompt hashing - do you need raw prompts or hashed pointers?
[00:01:36] Anita Patel: hashed pointers are fine, we cannot store raw prompts with PII in them. hashing with a salt that we manage is preferable. also timestamps need to be in UTC and iso format for our SIEM ingestion.
[00:01:48] Priya Nandakumar: ok we can switch to salted sha256 of prompt text and include salt id as metadata so you can verify offline. timestamps are iso8601 UTC by default but i'll confirm formatting in the log sample.

[00:02:20] Jordan Lee: i'll also add in the notes - jordan will share a redacted sample of the audit logs that shows the fields, and priya will update the logging config.

[00:02:36] Carlos Ramirez: on retention, we had originally asked for seven days for the pilot, but legal wants that in writing - what retention does redwood default to for hosted trials?
[00:02:46] Priya Nandakumar: default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs unless a different retention is negotiated; for dedicated/private deployments you can set custom retention and we can do 7 days for pilot on the hosted instance as a special config, but we need to document it in the SOW.

[00:03:02] Michael O'Neill: is there any risk if we drop to 7 days? like for debugging or quality regressions?
[00:03:08] Priya Nandakumar: you will lose older trace history; we recommend exporting important traces to your S3 if you need longer-term observability. but for compliance pilot, 7 days is fine if you capture samples you want to keep. we also have the option to keep hashed prompts and metadata longer and delete text fields earlier.

[00:03:30] Anita Patel: hashed prompts + metadata longer, raw text removal quicker, that fits our compliance ask. please provide the exact retention policy text so we can include in our security questionnaire.

[00:03:45] Jordan Lee: noted, i'll draft that clause and include the timeline and an export procedure.

[00:04:20] Zoe Kim: network question - priya i tried the VPC peering setup and hit a routing issue when spinning up the dedicated test node, connection times out to the peered subnet. any hints?
[00:04:28] Priya Nandakumar: did you update the security groups? our peering needs the egress rules to allow 443 and the ephemeral ports for kv/cache sync. also need the NACL rules to allow established responses. i can share the exact terraform snippet.

[00:04:46] Zoe Kim: yea i think the NACL blocked the response, will re-open and test. can you send a minimal firewall ruleset?

[00:04:56] Priya Nandakumar: absolutely, i'll send the runbook; i'll also include a diagram of the subnet CIDR mapping.

[00:05:20] Carlos Ramirez: another big question is SSO. we attempted an IdP connection yesterday and got an error around assertion mappings; how far are we from full SAML SSO for the pilot?
[00:05:30] Jordan Lee: priya?
[00:05:32] Priya Nandakumar: so we have SAML SSO support in the console; for pilots we usually do SAML v2 with email->username mapping and we support both signed assertions and encrypted assertions. the issue you're hitting is likely the NameID format; your IdP is sending persistent vs email. we can accept either, just need the attribute mapping adjusted.

[00:05:50] Anita Patel: we require SAML signed assertions and want session expiration of max 1 hour; can you confirm session timeout control from your side?

[00:05:58] Priya Nandakumar: session expiry is configurable per organization on the control plane; default is 8 hours but we can set it down to 1 hour for Meridian. i will confirm the exact config path in the admin console.

[00:06:20] Jordan Lee: we'll also send the SSO metadata xml you can import into your IdP and a sample attribute mapping.

[00:06:42] Michael O'Neill: about audit trails for admin actions - we need to see who changed config, who kicked off a model rollout, etc. how granular are your admin audit logs?

[00:06:52] Priya Nandakumar: we log admin actions with actor, action, timestamp, object, and before/after for config changes. those are available via the audit API and are forwarded to SIEM via our syslog connector or S3 export. note that the detailed before/after payloads can be redacted if they include sensitive fields.

[00:07:18] Anita Patel: redaction is important. our policy says we cannot retain credentials or secret keys in change payloads. how do you handle that?

[00:07:26] Priya Nandakumar: we redact credential fields server-side, and we don't store raw secrets in the audit logs. the change payload will show a placeholder like <REDACTED> and an attribute indicating the field name.

[00:07:38] Carlos Ramirez: good. on encryption - do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) on the hosted offering or only for private deployments?

[00:07:46] Jordan Lee: current hosted offering supports envelope encryption with provider-managed keys; CMK support is available on Dedicated and Private deployments. for pilots we can sign an agreement to use a bring-your-own-key path if we move to a dedicated pilot node.

[00:08:01] Anita Patel: we need KMS integration for any PII handling. can you confirm timeline to get a dedicated node with CMK enabled?

[00:08:08] Priya Nandakumar: provisioning a dedicated node takes about 2-3 weeks once SOW is signed; enabling CMK is a configuration step that runs in parallel and typically 2-4 business days after the instance is ready. so end-to-end 3-4 weeks.

[00:08:24] Michael O'Neill: that's ok but procurement is trying to speed up the timeline. we'll flag as a risk in our internal plan.

[00:08:45] Jordan Lee: switching to SOC2 - customer asked for SOC2 Type II evidence. we can share a SOC2 Type II summary and a redacted report under NDA. i'll share the summary doc after the call and a link to the redacted report for review.

[00:09:00] Anita Patel: we do require the full report under a DPA or NDA, our legal team can't accept just the summary.

[00:09:07] Jordan Lee: understood. i'll start the redaction process and have legal send you the NDA template.

[00:09:18] Priya Nandakumar: also we have a penetration test summary from last quarter, i'll attach that as well.

[00:09:28] Zoe Kim: for the pilot quality checks, we noticed one spike in latency during a batching window last night—do you have insight?
[00:09:36] Priya Nandakumar: probably the scheduler hit a large batch at the same time as a KV cache miss; i'll pull the logs and point to the batch size and the backoff. in the interim you can set a max_batch_size override on the route.

[00:09:50] Michael O'Neill: can you send the recommended route config so ops can apply?
[00:09:54] Priya Nandakumar: yes, i'll send a recommended config with explanation of tradeoffs for latency vs throughput.

[00:10:12] Anita Patel: one more on data residency — for the pilot we're ok to keep data in us-east-1 but for production we'll need eu-west-1. do you support region pinning?

[00:10:20] Jordan Lee: yes we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private; hosted instances in the future will allow region selection per tenant. for this pilot we can pin the instance to us-east-1 since your data must stay in the US for the pilot.

[00:10:36] Carlos Ramirez: legal asked about subprocessor list—who are your cloud providers and any third-party monitoring tools?

[00:10:42] Jordan Lee: primary cloud providers are AWS and GCP for different clusters; subprocessors include our metrics provider (Datadog), SSO provider (Okta is optional), and our build artifact store. i'll share the updated subprocessor list with contact points.

[00:11:05] Anita Patel: do you support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning? we want SCIM for automated deprovisioning.

[00:11:10] Priya Nandakumar: yes, SCIM v2 is supported for user provisioning and group sync; we also support SCIM-driven deprovisioning hooks. we'll share the SCIM endpoint and sample payload.

[00:11:34] Michael O'Neill: ok looks like we have a solid path forward. can we quickly recap owners?
[00:11:40] Jordan Lee: sure. recap:
- Jordan will share SOC2 summary & redacted report request and the retention policy text.
- Priya will send VPC peering runbook, firewall rules, SCIM/SSO metadata, route config recommendations, and pen test summary.
- Anita will confirm retention window and stakeholder requirements for sensitive logs.
- Michael to surface procurement/legal contacts and timeline.

[00:12:18] Carlos Ramirez: timeline wise we want decision by Oct 20 for next phase, and we'd like a security onsite the week of Oct 13 if possible.

[00:12:28] Jordan Lee: noted, i'll coordinate with our security team and propose two slots for onsite.

[00:12:40] Zoe Kim: quick question — are you able to add an allowlist of IPs for the admin console? we want to limit admin console to our corp IP range.

[00:12:48] Priya Nandakumar: yes, we support admin console IP allowlists per org. i'll include the config snippet.

[00:13:08] Anita Patel: also can you confirm if audit logs include the actor's UPN or just a unique user id? we need both for correlation with our identity store.

[00:13:16] Priya Nandakumar: we can include actor_upn and actor_id in the audit records. we'll show both in the sample.

[00:13:40] Jordan Lee: any blockers we didn't cover?
[00:13:45] Michael O'Neill: none from my side, just dependency on the SOC2 NDA and the retention confirmation.
[00:13:52] Carlos Ramirez: same here.

[00:14:05] Jordan Lee: ok great. last note — i'll follow up after the call with a single thread containing SOC2 link, VPC runbook, SAML metadata and the recommended route config. please flag anything that's incorrect in the first 48 hours.

[00:14:20] Priya Nandakumar: i'll also create a short runbook for your devs to adjust max_batch_size and kv cache TTL if you want to test immediate mitigations for latency spikes.

[00:14:40] Liam Ortiz: i'll set up the calendar invite for an onsite security review and loop in our security lead.

[00:15:00] Carlos Ramirez: thanks everyone.
[00:15:02] Jordan Lee: thanks — we'll close the call.

Note: transcript above has been lightly cleaned for readability but retains some speech artifacts and minor transcription errors typical of automated meeting exports.
